q-90945.name: Question 1
q-90945.problem: Find the real solution to the equation $2(x+4)^{3}=686.$
q-90945.worked_solution:
We can solve this equation by isolating the $(x+4)^{3}$ term and then taking the $3$rd root of each side.

First, let's isolate the $(x+4)^{3}$ term on the left-hand side:

$$
\begin{aligned}2(x+4)^{3} & =686 \\ (x+4)^{3} & =343\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we take the $3$rd root of each side and solve for $x.$ Since $n=3$ is odd, there is only one real solution to this equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}(x+4)^{3} & =343 \\ \sqrt[3]{(x+4)^{3}} & =\sqrt[3]{343} \\ x+4 & =\sqrt[3]{{7}^{3}} \\ x+4 & =7 \\ x & =3\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution is $x=3.$

q-91348.name: Question 2
q-91348.problem: Find the real solution to the equation ${x}^{7}=-\frac{1}{128}.$
q-91348.worked_solution:
We can solve this equation by taking the $7$th root of each side and solving for $x.$ Since $n=7$ is odd, there is only one real solution to this equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{7} & =-\frac{1}{128} \\ \sqrt[7]{{x}^{7}} & =\sqrt[7]{(-\frac{1}{128})} \\ x & =\sqrt[7]{{(-\frac{1}{2})}^{7}} \\ x & =-\frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution is $x=-\frac{1}{2}.$

q-91369.name: Question 3
q-91369.problem: Find the real solution to the equation $(x-3)^{7}=-128.$
q-91369.worked_solution:
We can solve this equation by taking the $7$th root of each side and solving for $x.$
Since $n=7$ is odd, there is only one real solution to this equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}(x-3)^{7} & =-128 \\ \sqrt[7]{(x-3)^{7}} & =\sqrt[7]{-128} \\ x-3 & =\sqrt[7]{(-2)^{7}} \\ x-3 & =-2 \\ x & =1\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution is $x=1.$
